questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country in Europe and due to Brexit my choice became Dublin. Also because of former recommendations.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a great stay overall. Due to corona there were some optical meeting new people in the begining and we had to to a lot out self to meet people. Trinity weren't very helpfull with that due to corona.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright. The staff was really friendly and helpfull, though a bit slow due to a more old fashioned way of doing things.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received our login to TCD and through there waited for more information on classes, studentcard and so on. Not all of us student received the information at the same time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was not the best. It wasn't really a welcomst. There were no social things planned for the Eramus students, only Freshers, who were probably priotized because of corona. You had to "book" a spot for all the activities, even getting a tour on campus, but you needed a promo code which we did not receive.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough if you begin early and are ready to pay a suuuuper high rent. It costed around 8500 kr. per month. But the place was great though. I lived at Beckett House which I found through Aparto Student housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Beckett House I recommend as it is a fun dorm room. I used a lot of time there and meet most of friends there. A lot of Trinity students living there. Priotize modern falitices and the social aspect over a lower rent, I think it will be the best desicion in the end.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you are willing to pay you'll find a nice place in walking distance to Trinity and the city center, though most student accommodation are in the more schehty areas of Dublin. I highly recommend staying close to the city as you will go to campus, go out ect. a lot daily almost.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a slow process in the beginning, but when it finally worked, it was easy enough.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You will get contacted for which steps you need to take. The order for registration is a bit random which is a bit frustrating. However, they are always very helpfull towards you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Academic Registry had a hotline for help which is where I got most of my help/information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted and there is a thinking period before the classes a finale, which gives to time and options to switch which was really helpfull for me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be patience, read everything they send you carefully.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great and motivated professors. Interactive classes. Not a lot of reading. Not a whole lot of classes to chose between though. Only undergraduate classes even though you are a postgraduate student, but I knew that beforehand.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were easier than Danish classes. An entirely way of learning, discussing, talking, writing and so on. Rather interesting and I learned a lot by trying this.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mainly big lectures where the professor would talk. Some lectures there would be discussion but otherwise no group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Food law, Medical law and Ethics, European Human Rights law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i recommend them all. They are all essay based which I liked. However, I had to write six essays in around the two lasts months which ended being a lot of stress. However, very good and passionated professors, who were also very friendly towards Eramus students and understanding of our different situation. Medical law was a lot more fun and different than expected, however it is common law about Ireland, so maybe not entirely useful.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I travelled a lot and did a lot of social activities which took most of my budget.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in general were cheap. Itmens like wine were expensive. Normal stuff like shampoo and so on was cheap. The only thing really surprisingly was the really expensive rent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many clubs. I enrolled in a lot. However, after 1,5 year lockdown, it was hard getting a spot for things and events as everyone wanted to join. The hiking club looked great though. Most clubs have weekly/monthly activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kind of sports, language, food, acting, nature and so on. More than 200 clubs so almost everything you possible can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the hiking club. Otherwise the cancer society has a good cause. and the food society gives discounts of foods.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Dublin and ireland is full of possibility. Great hikes both close and far from Dublin. A great range of cosy pubs. Great and free museums.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was only difficult the first few days. Ireland is a lot more different from Denmark than first expected. But it felt like home really quick and I felt comftobel in the environment.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: WhatsApp groups for social stuff are great. Live in a dorm room and enjoy that and try to meet people there through social activities. Try to just talk to people you meet in classes, clubs, events, housing and so on. Difficult at first but people are very friendly and open minded.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of barriers with time, money and hobbies from people from the north to the south of europe. Did not expect this to take up to much space in social gatherings and activities.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Irish charm and friendly is great. Ireland makes you feel home and welcome (probably unlike Denmark at most times).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy this time so much and try to go to the country side as much a possible. Both plan and be spontan - the best nights meeting new friends happen while being spontaneous, however the best weekend trips were planned some weeks before.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take a chance and do it. Trinity and Ireland is both fun, colorfull and beautiful. however, surprised how dirty and smelly Dublin could be in some areas.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to meet new people and cultures and focus on personal growth through this. Also getting better and more comfortable speaking enligsh.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I meet a lot of people, hiked and travelled many weekends, the pub culture - there are many great aspects.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If in doubt - please go! Trinity was a once in a lifetime experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
